title: Bribing an enlarged coordinate set
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, let $J$ be a set of coordinates, let $i$ be a coordinate, and let $b\in\{-1,1\}$. For every input $x$, bribing the coordinates in $J\cup\{i\}$ to $b$ gives the same output as first setting coordinate $i$ of $x$ to $b$ and then bribing the coordinates in $J$ to $b$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$i$ is a coordinate (with no requirement that $i\notin J$)
the identity holds for every input
